scientific_question: Do the two sparse sign rescues from the initial local-support ablation recur when the exact design is rerun on a non-overlapping stochastic block?
decision_rule: If reproduction sign rescue recurs (>0), call network-context sign buffering replicated but quantify bidirectionality/worsening separately.
If sign rescue is 0 but magnitude rescue persists, call local support a robust magnitude/branch allocator without replicated sign buffering.
If rescue disappears and worsening dominates, downgrade the network-context buffer interpretation further.
forbidden: do not change support strength after seeing the initial two sign rescues
do not search seed blocks until sign rescue appears
do not pool blocks before reporting each separately
do not use Guaiacum or other empirical outcomes to set thresholds or seeds
claim_boundary: This robustness block tests synthetic network-context capability only and cannot empirically admit service redundancy.
